About

Hi, I’m Jack.

I’m a UX researcher based in the Southwest. I want to help companies build intuitive, connected and accessible experiences, online and in person, from a real understanding of their customers’ behaviors, preferences and needs.

Background

I’m an Eagle Scout, and I earned a B.A. in Psychology with a minor in Sociology from the University of Arizona. In my senior year I realized the questions I cared about most, why people do what they do and what gets in their way, are the same ones a good product has to answer.

So after graduating I completed PeakXD’s international UX research and design program, worked with real clients, and earned my BCS Foundation Certificate in User Experience and the IBM Data Science Professional Certificate.

Why research first

I enjoy every part of the design process, but I want to start by going deep on research. You can’t design well for people until you’ve walked in their shoes and understand how they live, what they prefer and what they need. Psychology and sociology taught me to look for the reasons behind what people do, and research is where I get to use that every day.

Why accessibility is personal

My grandmother has macular degeneration.

The condition takes away the center of your vision, the part you use to read and pick out detail. Seeing what that does to everyday things online, like small text, faint buttons and crowded pages, is what got me interested in how people with disabilities experience the web. It’s the part of UX I most want to grow in.

When I look at a design, I start with her in mind:

  • Text people can read without zooming in
  • Contrast that holds up for low vision
  • Layouts that make sense without fine detail

My work so far

It’s early in my UX career, and I’ve already had the chance to apply what I learned with three real clients, plus my current role.

  1. Veeam Software · Tempe, AZ 2025 – now Site Experience Specialist. I survey employees about their time in the office and turn the findings into changes to the workplace.
  2. Premier Packout · Scottsdale, AZ 2024 – 25 With the CEO of a fire and flood pack-out company, I mapped how homeowners experience a pack-out and turned the pain points into a service plan. Read the case study
  3. Origins Cannabis · Redmond, WA 2022 – 23 I interviewed customers in the store to learn why the app failed them, then rebuilt its product display and tested it. Read the case study
  4. Oxfam Australia · Remote 2022 For my PeakXD certification project, I redesigned Oxfam’s support pages and MyOxfam portal, from interviews to a tested final design. Read the case study

Before UX

Before UX, I worked as a lifeguard, a swim instructor, and a shift lead and trainer. Those jobs, along with scouting, taught me to learn quickly, solve problems, lead, coach, teach and work well with other people. I also speak some Spanish and Italian.

What I’m looking for

A UX research role, or a research-heavy design role, at a company that builds with its users instead of guessing about them. I want to go deep on research first and grow into design from there.
